rulings.R1: Seg 1 now ends: 'It is the lesson for any model that predicts a number, whether spend or what a new lead will be worth: the columns you feed it and the scale you fit it on matter more than a cleverer algorithm.' The recap says 'a number model' and 'a yes or no question'.

rulings.specific: Three ideas: (1) the baseline ladder, segs 1-3 and the ladder card in seg 6; (2) why raw dollars mislead and the log scale, seg 4, result in seg 6; (3) typical versus average, seg 7. The zero-spend row filter has its own short segment (5) before the ladder card. The brief makes four plain asks. 'Two errors cancel' is dropped. To make room, the old segment 6 (log weights as percentages, with the effects table) became one spoken sentence and a line in the ladder note. 899 spoken words. The two sets of total-error figures: regression.typical_vs_average (-3.6%, +0.1%, x1.039) is attached to the 3,473 test advertisers who kept spending in the narration, the card title and the card sub; regression.models.*.total_error (all 4,000) appears once, +6.1% for the corrected log model, in quiz q2's explanation with the words 'over all 4,000'; the +2.1% figure is left out.
